checked: tools/build_site.py --check (run separately by CI; reports current)

findings.title: Published ladder is a partial view of the book
findings.detail: The reported total depth is larger than the sum of the levels printed in the same payload, and one row's top-of-book total disagrees with its first level. The ladder is monotonic and every level is within $0.00-$1.00, so this is a display-truncation issue rather than a corrupt quote — but a page must not print the ladder total and the depth total as if they were the same number.
findings.action: Recompute from the raw payload or blank the derived field.

findings.title: Estimated 24h notional was computed from a different price than the row prints
findings.detail: 24h volume x the row's own price differs from the printed estimate on 13 row(s); the largest gap is 10.7%. The implied price is the previous mid, so the notional was fixed before the row's quote was refreshed.
findings.action: Recompute the estimate after the final quote is applied, or label it as measured at an earlier time. The direction of the number is unaffected; the exact dollar figure is.

findings.title: Status values match the documented lifecycle
findings.detail: Observed: active. The lifecycle page lists these statuses and maps the open/settled request filters onto active/finalized.

findings.title: Research-desk capture comes from the production root
findings.detail: rest_base is https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2, while the brief asks for the demo environment and the Node board's capture uses the demo root. Production and demo catalogues and quotes differ (https://docs.kalshi.com/getting_started/demo_env), so a page mixing the two must say which is which.
findings.action: Label the environment on every page that renders this capture, as the live desk does in /api/meta.

findings.title: The Node generator's --check can never pass as written
findings.detail: `scripts/build-site.mjs --check` re-renders every page and compares the result with the committed file, but the render embeds a fresh `data-generated` timestamp and relative text such as '21m ago'. Every page therefore reports stale within a minute of generation. The data itself matched when this audit compared it.
findings.action: Compare the page with the timestamp and relative-time fields normalised, or drop the strict comparison from the gate. CI does not currently run this check.
